LARCH 501: Landscape architectural research methods and writing techniques.
LARCH 502: Introductory theory seminar covering the intellectual history of landscape architecture and theoretical contributions from related disciplines.
LARCH 503: This graduate seminar explores contemporary theoretical frameworks and literature in landscape architecture since 2000, with a focus on landscape epistemology, ecological design, systems thinking, biodiversity, climate resilience, environmental justice, and digital technologies.
LARCH 504: Landscape architecture is a discipline that crosses multiple realms, including the natural and social sciences, the humanities, and the arts.
LARCH 510: Landscape architectural theory exploration through readings and discussions.
LARCH 515: Introductory landscape architectural design and applied theory for MLA students.
LARCH 550: The final capstone studio for students completing the Master of Landscape Architecture.
LARCH 551: The Final Culminating Experience Proposal course provides the opportunity for a student to develop an area of inquiry within the discipline of landscape architecture to be explored toward the production of a capstone project as the final culminating experience of the Master of Landscape Architecture degree.
LARCH 552: Following approval of the FCE proposal (LARCH 551), students shall proceed to implement their research project based on their prepared schedule.
LARCH 553: In this course students shall prepare final documentation of their research-based design project, and make a public presentation/defense of their project's relevance, research/inquiry methods, design approach, and findings.
LARCH 590: Continuing seminars which consist of a series of individual lectures by faculty, students, or outside speakers.
LARCH 596: Independent study opportunities open for graduate students covering topics which fall oustide the scope of formal courses (non thesis).
LARCH 597: Formal courses given on a topical or special interest subject which may be offered infrequently.
LARCH 815: LARCH 815 is the first of a three-course sequence of design studios at the core of the professional M.L.A.
LARCH 816: LARCH 816 considers the broader landscape and systems within the landscape.
LARCH 817: LARCH 817 provides an overview of community and spatial design that accommodates civic and public functions while addressing social and environmental imperatives.
LARCH 835: Computer Applications for Site Analysis and Design.
LARCH 836: The landscape architect calls upon a rich array of materials to construct the built elements of landscape walls, ground surfaces, overhead structures, and furniture systems.
LARCH 837: This course addresses the applied principles, tools, and techniques of planting design implementation, with a focus on landscape planting methods and technically proficient documentation.
LARCH 838: This course is one of four graduate-level design implementation offerings that focus upon the more technical aspects of landscape architectural practice.
